input_sentence: The New York Knicks pulled off a dramatic comeback in the NBA Finals on June 11, 2026, taking a nearly insurmountable lead.
headline: Knicks Complete Largest Comeback in NBA Finals History, Lead Spurs 3-1
dek: OG Anunoby's tip-in with 1.2 seconds left capped a 29-point comeback as New York puts San Antonio on the brink of elimination.
summary: The New York Knicks overcame a 29-point deficit to defeat the San Antonio Spurs 107-106 in Game 4 of the 2026 NBA Finals on June 11, the largest comeback in NBA Finals history. OG Anunoby tipped in a missed Jalen Brunson three-pointer with 1.2 seconds remaining to seal the win at Madison Square Garden. The Knicks now lead the best-of-seven series 3-1 and are one win away from their first championship since 1973. Game 5 is scheduled for Saturday, June 13 in San Antonio.

key_facts.value: Knicks overcame a 29-point deficit — the largest comeback in NBA Finals history, surpassing the Celtics' 24-point comeback vs. Lakers in 2008

key_facts.value: OG Anunoby tip-in with 1.2 seconds remaining gave Knicks a 107-106 lead

key_facts.value: Knicks trailed 76-49 at half — the largest halftime deficit for a home team in Finals history

key_facts.value: Jalen Brunson led all scorers with 36 points and gave Knicks their first lead at 105-104 with 1:22 remaining

key_facts.label: Anunoby's performance
key_facts.value: OG Anunoby scored 33 points on 10-for-15 shooting, including 7-of-9 from three, plus the game-winning tip-in and a critical block

key_facts.label: Wembanyama's line
key_facts.value: Victor Wembanyama scored 24 points and grabbed 13 rebounds for San Antonio but shot 9-for-25 overall

key_facts.label: Win probability
key_facts.value: With 9:33 remaining, ESPN Analytics gave the Spurs a 99.6% win probability — a 1-in-250 chance for the Knicks

key_facts.label: Championship drought
key_facts.value: A Knicks title would be their first since 1973 — closing the longest gap between championships in NBA history

why_it_matters: The Knicks are one win away from their first NBA championship since 1973 — which would close the longest title drought in franchise history and the longest gap between championships in NBA history. The Game 4 comeback itself is already cemented as the greatest in Finals history, instantly iconic in New York sports lore. For the young Spurs, led by 22-year-old Victor Wembanyama, squandering a 29-point lead has exposed costly inexperience on the game's biggest stage at the worst possible moment.

extras.format_summary: The NBA Finals is a best-of-seven series between the Eastern Conference champion New York Knicks and Western Conference champion San Antonio Spurs. The first team to win four games claims the title.
extras.how_to_watch: Games on ABC and ESPN; also streaming on fubo.

reactions.take: Called the Spurs 'the dumbest basketball team in the history of civilisation' after they blew the 29-point lead, saying San Antonio's mismanagement actively helped the Knicks win.
Said he couldn't explain the collapse: 'I think it's just execution, greediness of some sort. We clearly weren't the most hungry in the second half.'
Credited team belief: 'One word that caps that all is just belief. It was chipping away, one possession at a time. It wasn't going to be one play to get us back.'
Declared: 'What we witnessed in New York on Wednesday night was nothing short of the greatest comeback in NBA history.'
Called it 'the most stunning game I've ever seen.'
Called Anunoby's putback 'the most iconic shot in the history of New York basketball.'
Revealed he was shouting from the sidelines coming out of the final timeout: 'The offensive rebound is there! The offensive rebound is there! Somebody go!'
Exclaimed: 'Knicks, you are the NBA Champs! Spurs, are you kidding me??'
Nearly fell onto the court in disbelief after Josh Hart lost control of a would-be go-ahead layup, going viral as one of the most captured fan moments of the night.
The lifelong Knicks fan was caught on camera in tears in the backseat of a car on the way home after the win.

56 people were taken into custody — 15 arrested, 41 given summonses — after rowdy post-game crowds took over streets near MSG, climbed on vehicles, lit fireworks, and injured 10 officers. A planned official watch party had been abruptly cancelled earlier that day amid a dispute between MSG CEO James Dolan and city officials.

whats_next: Game 5 in San Antonio on Saturday, June 13 (8:30 p.m. ET, ABC/fubo) — Knicks can clinch their first championship since 1973; Spurs must win to stay alive.
Watch for Wembanyama's response: the Spurs star has been the biggest Finals factor when the series has gone San Antonio's way, and he'll need a dominant closeout-game performance to force Game 6.
Monitor NYPD presence around MSG: authorities have pledged increased security after arrests at watch parties for Games 2, 3, and 4; a potential clinching celebration could draw massive crowds.
The Finals MVP race: Anunoby leads the ladder, but Brunson and Wembanyama could leapfrog him depending on who stars in the elimination game.
If the Spurs win Game 5, the series returns to New York for Game 6 on Tuesday, June 16.
